Its appeal lies in the abundant lingering snow, with snowfields remaining even in summer, and the alpine flower fields coloring its ridges. Because it lies deep in remote mountains, the climb takes several days, but magnificent scenery awaits as a reward.
quiz_en: If you were hiking the ridges of Mount Iide, which would you look forward to more: the summer snowfields or the alpine flowers?

desc_en: You have arrived at Mikagura Onsen in Hirotani, Aga Town. This mountain onsen (hot spring) at the foot of Mount Mikagura lets you enjoy the bath in quiet natural surroundings. Aga Town is a town with mountain villages dotted along the Agano River, wrapped in deep snow in winter. Stop by after hiking or a walk along the mountain streams, and rest your body slowly in the mountain hot spring.
quiz_en: While soaking in a mountain onsen like this one, which sound of nature would you be happiest to hear around you?

desc_en: You have arrived at the Kirinzan Castle ruins in Tsugawa, Aga Town. These are the remains of a mountain castle built atop Mount Kirin, rising at the confluence of the Agano and Tokonami rivers, which controlled a key route linking Aizu and Echigo. The mountain, with cliffs dropping to the river, is also known as a scenic spot. Tsugawa is a town with legends of foxes, and every spring a fox wedding procession is held.
quiz_en: In the town of Tsugawa at the foot of Mount Kirin, what fox-themed procession is held every spring?

desc_en: You have arrived at Nakanosawa Gorge Forest Park in Aga Town. This forest park, laid out along a mountain gorge, lets you spend time surrounded by a clear stream and green forest. In summer you can enjoy playing in the river and camping, and in autumn walks among the colored leaves, making it a place to feel close to nature. Listen to the murmuring stream and savor the quiet of Aga's mountain villages.
quiz_en: If you spent time at a gorge forest park like this one, which would you enjoy more: playing in the river or camping?

desc_en: You have arrived at Mount Mikagura in Aga Town. This mountain near the border between Niigata and Fukushima is known among climbers as a rock mountain of Echigo for its rugged form with sheer rock walls. Reaching the summit takes stamina, but the ridges offer a grand view of the surrounding mountains. In the sound of its name, which tells of a mountain god dancing kagura (sacred dance), you can sense the mystery of this deep mountain land.
quiz_en: If you climbed a mountain with sheer rock walls rising around you, what view would you most want to see from the summit?

desc_en: You have arrived at the Ogi castle ruins in Izumozaki Town. Izumozaki is a port town on the Sea of Japan that prospered in the Edo period as the port where gold and silver from Sado were unloaded onto the mainland, and it also thrived as a post town on the Hokkoku Kaido highway. It is also known as the birthplace of Ryokan. Visit the castle ruins in the hills and feel the depth of this port town's history.
quiz_en: Who was the Edo-period monk, born in Izumozaki, who is said to have played with temari balls together with local children?

desc_en: You have arrived at Mount Tanigawa in Yuzawa Town. This mountain rising on the border between Niigata and Gunma is one of Japan's 100 Famous Mountains. Its rugged rock faces, exemplified by the great wall of Ichinokurasawa, have attracted many climbers. From the Gunma side you can ride a ropeway partway up, and from the twin peaks of the summit you can take in the mountains along the Joshu-Echigo border.
quiz_en: The summit of Mount Tanigawa has two peaks standing side by side, so what is a mountain with this kind of shape called?

desc_en: You have arrived at the wetlands around the summit of Mount Naeba in Yuzawa Town. The summit of Mount Naeba forms a gentle plateau covered in wetlands dotted with countless small ponds. It is said that these ponds, which look like rice paddies, are the origin of the mountain's name, Naeba (seedling field). Walk the boardwalks and in summer alpine flowers bloom, revealing scenery like a paradise in the sky.
quiz_en: What are the small pond-like pools of water called that dot the wetlands on the summit of Mount Naeba?

desc_en: You have arrived at the Owara Kaze no Bon in Yatsuo, Toyama City. Held every year from September 1 to 3, it sees dancers with straw hats pulled low over their faces dance quietly through the sloping streets. The melancholy tunes of Etchu Owara-bushi, played on the kokyu and shamisen, echo through the night town, while the light of paper lanterns creates a dreamlike atmosphere.
quiz_en: In the music of Owara Kaze no Bon, what bowed stringed instrument plays sorrowful tones together with the shamisen?

desc_en: You have arrived to see the mirages of Toyama Bay. From spring to early summer, the temperature difference between cold seawater and warm air causes a mysterious phenomenon in which the towns and ships on the opposite shore appear stretched or upside down. Toyama Bay has long been known as a famous mirage spot, and the coast of Uozu is particularly well known as a viewing place. If you are lucky, you may encounter this phantom scenery.
quiz_en: During which season of the year are mirages most likely to be seen over Toyama Bay, especially from the coast of Uozu?

desc_en: You have arrived at Kumonotaira in the Northern Alps. This lava plateau lies deep among the mountains surrounding the headwaters of the Kurobe River, and because it takes a long journey from any trailhead, it is also called Japan's last unexplored wilderness. Boardwalks stretch across the plateau, alpine flowers bloom in summer, and famous peaks encircle it. This is the scenery of a paradise above the clouds that only those who make it here can see.
quiz_en: Kumonotaira lies deep in the Northern Alps and is very hard to reach, so what is it often called because of this?

desc_en: You have arrived at Mount Yakushi in Toyama City. Rising 2,926 meters in the central Northern Alps, it is counted among Japan's 100 Famous Mountains. On its eastern face, several landforms called cirques, carved out by glaciers, line up and are designated a Special Natural Monument. Its massive form and magnificent ridge walks captivate climbers.
quiz_en: What are the bowl-shaped landforms called that were carved out by glaciers and line up along the eastern face of Mount Yakushi?

desc_en: You have arrived at the Hakuba Sanzan in the northern Northern Alps. Made up of three peaks, Mount Shirouma, Mount Shakushi and Mount Hakuba Yari, they line the border between Toyama and Nagano. In summer, alpine flower fields spread along the ridges, and the Hakuba Daisekkei snowfield on the Nagano side is a popular route for climbers. Traverse all three peaks and you can fully enjoy the grand views of the Northern Alps.
quiz_en: The Hakuba Sanzan are made up of three peaks, so besides Mount Shirouma and Mount Hakuba Yari, what is the third one?

desc_en: You have arrived at Kurobe Gorge. Carved deep through the Northern Alps by the Kurobe River, it is one of Japan's foremost V-shaped gorges, with sheer rock walls towering on both banks. The trolley train runs from Unazuki Onsen to Keyakidaira, letting you view the emerald stream as you pass over iron bridges and through tunnels. In autumn the mountainsides are dyed with colorful leaves, wrapping the whole gorge in magnificent color.
quiz_en: What is the name of the small train that carries sightseers from Unazuki Onsen deep into Kurobe Gorge?

desc_en: You have arrived at the Johana Hikiyama Festival in Nanto City. Held every May as the festival of Johana Shinmeigu Shrine, it features hikiyama floats adorned with lavish carvings and lacquer touring the town. From the iori-yatai stalls leading the floats, stylish iori-uta songs flow along with flutes and shamisen. Registered as part of the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Yama, Hoko, Yatai float festivals, it is the splendid festival of a town that prospered through silk weaving.
quiz_en: At the Johana Hikiyama Festival, what are the songs called that flow from the iori-yatai stalls with flute and shamisen accompaniment?

desc_en: You have arrived at the Gokayama gassho-zukuri villages in Nanto City. The two villages of Ainokura and Suganuma are registered as a World Cultural Heritage site together with Shirakawa-go in Gifu Prefecture. Houses with steep thatched roofs nestle together in the mountains, becoming a dreamlike scene wrapped in snow in winter. Gokayama is also known for washi paper making and the folk song Kokiriko-bushi, and traditional wisdom for living lives on here.
quiz_en: What folk song from Gokayama, danced while sounding the sasara clapper, is said to be one of the oldest folk songs in Japan?

desc_en: You have arrived at Mount Tsurugi in Kamiichi Town. At 2,999 meters, this rugged rocky peak, also called a temple of rock and snow, is a mountain Japanese climbers long to climb. When a Meiji-era survey team reached the summit, they reportedly found the head of an old monk's staff and other items, an episode depicted in the novel and film Tsurugidake: Ten no Ki. Its sharply soaring form overwhelms all who see it.
quiz_en: What is the title of the novel by Nitta Jiro depicting the Meiji-era survey team and the first recorded ascent of Mount Tsurugi?

desc_en: You have arrived at Kurobe Dam in Tateyama Town. Completed in the 1960s after an extremely difficult construction, this arch dam boasts the tallest embankment in Japan. During the sightseeing water discharge held from summer to autumn, over ten tons of water per second gush out with a roar, and rainbows sometimes appear in the spray. As a highlight of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, it attracts many travelers.
quiz_en: What is the event called, held at Kurobe Dam from summer to autumn, in which water gushes out powerfully for visitors to see?

desc_en: You have arrived to see the raicho (rock ptarmigan) of Tateyama. The ptarmigan is a bird of the alpine zone designated a Special Natural Monument, and the area around Murodo on Tateyama is known as a good place to encounter it. It changes its plumage to mottled brown in summer and pure white in winter, protecting itself from predators. Seeing one appear from the shade of creeping pines along the trail is a reward for visitors to the high mountains.
quiz_en: The rock ptarmigan of Tateyama is a Special Natural Monument, so what color do its feathers change to when winter arrives?

desc_en: You have arrived at Shomyo Falls in Tateyama Town. Plunging from the Midagahara plateau of Tateyama, it boasts a drop of about 350 meters, the highest in Japan, and is one of Japan's 100 Best Waterfalls. The water falls in four stages with a thunderous roar, and in the snowmelt season its volume increases, making it even more powerful. From spring to early summer, Hannoki Falls appears beside it, and two streams fall side by side.
quiz_en: Shomyo Falls on Tateyama boasts the greatest drop of any waterfall in Japan, so roughly how many meters is that drop?

desc_en: You have arrived at Tateyama. Along with Mount Fuji and Mount Hakusan, it is one of Japan's Three Holy Mountains, a collective name for peaks centered on Mount Onanji, the highest, and Mount Oyama. Using the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route, you can ride up to Murodo at about 2,450 meters, and in spring the Yuki no Otani (Great Snow Valley) appears, with towering walls of snow. At the summit of Oyama stands the summit shrine of Oyama Shrine.
quiz_en: On the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route in spring, what is the road called that runs between towering walls of snow?

desc_en: You have arrived at the Higashi Chaya District of Kanazawa. This teahouse district was opened in the Edo period with the permission of the Kaga domain, and beautiful townhouses with red-ocher lattices line its stone-paved streets. It is designated a national Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings. At dusk you may even hear the sound of the shamisen. Browsing shops selling sweets and crafts made with Kanazawa's famous gold leaf is another pleasure.
quiz_en: What are the fine wooden lattices called that can be seen on the windows of the townhouses in the Higashi Chaya District?

desc_en: You have arrived at Myoryu-ji in Nomachi, Kanazawa City. This Nichiren-sect temple was built as a prayer hall for the Maeda family of the Kaga domain and is known by its nickname, the Ninja Temple. Its interior is far more complex than its exterior suggests, with many devices said to have been designed against enemy intrusion, such as hidden staircases, pitfalls and lookout posts. Tours are guided and full of surprises.
quiz_en: Myoryu-ji is full of tricks such as hidden staircases and pitfalls, so what nickname is this temple commonly known by?

desc_en: You have arrived at Fushimi-ji in Teramachi, Kanazawa City. It stands in one corner of the Teramachi temple district spreading south of the Sai River. Many temples were gathered in Teramachi as part of the Kaga domain's castle town planning, and a calm townscape lined with numerous temples continues today. Walk the charming streets visiting the temples and feel the deep layers of history of the castle town of Kanazawa.
quiz_en: When walking through the Teramachi temple district of Kanazawa, what would you most like to pay attention to along the way?

desc_en: You have arrived at Yuwaku Onsen in Kanazawa City. This hot spring resort lies in the mountains beyond central Kanazawa and is called the inner retreat of Kanazawa. It has ties to Takehisa Yumeji, a Taisho-era painter and poet who stayed here, and the hot spring town has a memorial museum dedicated to him. Spend a relaxing time in the hot springs of this quiet mountain village.
quiz_en: Which painter, a leading figure of Taisho Romanticism, has ties to Yuwaku Onsen and a memorial museum there?

desc_en: You have arrived at Fukatani Onsen in Fukatanimachi, Kanazawa City. This onsen (hot spring) lies in a quiet suburb north of central Kanazawa. Kanazawa is a historic city that prospered as the castle town of the Kaga domain, famed for its wealth, and by going a little beyond sights like Kenroku-en and the teahouse districts, you can find calm hot springs like this. Between sightseeing, relax your body slowly in the bath.
quiz_en: After taking a break at a suburban onsen between sightseeing spots in Kanazawa, which famous place would you like to visit next?

desc_en: You have arrived at Kyokusui Onsen in Nanamagarimachi, Kanazawa City. This onsen (hot spring) is located in the hills heading from central Kanazawa toward the suburbs, with farmland and countryside scenery all around. The name Kyokusui, meaning winding stream, has an elegant ring to it. Rest your feet, tired from strolling the castle town, in the hot water and savor the relaxed air of the Kaga countryside.
quiz_en: If you could pick just one wagashi sweet unique to Kanazawa to enjoy after your bath, which one would you choose?

desc_en: You have arrived at Mount Akakura in Mihikimachi, Nanao City. This mountain in southern Nanao, facing Nanao Bay, has long been cherished by local people as a mountain of faith. Walking the tree-covered mountain, you will be wrapped in the calm atmosphere typical of Noto's satoyama. Gaze down at the villages from the mountain and feel the bond between Noto's nature and faith.
quiz_en: If you went walking in the satoyama countryside of Noto, in which season would you most enjoy the colors of the forest?

desc_en: You have arrived at Mount Bessho in Nakajima, Nanao City. This mountain in the middle of the Noto Peninsula has a service area on the Noto Satoyama Kaido expressway. From the observation deck you can look out over Notojima Island in Nanao Bay and the calm waters of the inner bay, and many people stop by during a drive. Take in a panorama typical of Noto, where countryside and sea blend together.
quiz_en: From the observation deck on Mount Bessho, which large island can you see floating in the waters of Nanao Bay?

desc_en: You have arrived at the Nanao Castle ruins in Nanao City. These are the remains of a huge mountain castle built in the Warring States period by the Hatakeyama clan, the military governors of Noto, and it is counted among Japan's five great mountain castles. It is also known for being captured by Uesugi Kenshin, and layers of stone walls remain on the mountain. From the main enclosure site you can look over Nanao Bay and Notojima, making it clear that this was a natural fortress.
quiz_en: Which clan built Nanao Castle and served as its lords while acting as the military governors of Noto in the Warring States period?

desc_en: You have arrived at Wakura Onsen in Nanao City. It is said to have begun when hot water gushed up from the sea of Nanao Bay, and it is Noto's representative hot spring resort. Large inns line the waterfront, and you can gaze at calm Nanao Bay and Notojima while soaking. The area suffered severe damage in the Noto Peninsula Earthquake, but it continues on its path toward recovery.
quiz_en: At Wakura Onsen facing Nanao Bay, at what time of day would you most like to gaze at the sea while soaking?

desc_en: You have arrived at Yukawa Onsen in Yukawamachi, Nanao City. Nanao is a port town on Nanao Bay near the base of the Noto Peninsula, long prospering as the center of Noto. Besides Wakura Onsen, the city has hot springs like this one, where you can enjoy the bath in the quiet of the countryside. Savor the simple warmth of the water along with seafood from the Noto coast.
quiz_en: If it were served at dinner in a hot spring inn in Noto, which seafood from Nanao Bay would make you happiest?

desc_en: You have arrived at Akasaki Onsen in Otamachi, Nanao City. This onsen (hot spring) sits near Nanao Bay, where you can feel close to the scenery of Noto's calm inland sea. Nanao Bay has gentle waves and is known as a rich sea, where oysters are farmed. Warm up slowly in the hot water of this seaside town and experience a way of life nurtured by Noto's land and sea.
quiz_en: Which shellfish, farmed widely in the calm waters of Nanao Bay in Noto, is at its best in the winter season?

desc_en: You have arrived at Natadera in Komatsu City. This ancient temple is said to have been founded by Taicho, who opened Mount Hakusan in the Nara period, and in its grounds rises a white rocky hill called Kigan Yusenkyo. Matsuo Basho stopped here on his journey of Oku no Hosomichi (The Narrow Road to the Deep North) and composed a haiku: whiter than the stones of Ishiyama, the autumn wind. In autumn, colored leaves adorn the strange rocks, making the grounds breathtakingly beautiful.
quiz_en: In the haiku Matsuo Basho composed at Natadera, which words follow the opening line, whiter than the stones of Ishiyama?

desc_en: You have arrived at the Okuradake Kogen highlands in Ogoya, Komatsu City. In southern Komatsu near the Hakusan mountains, these highlands are loved as a leisure spot for skiing in winter and camping and walking in summer. From the plateau you can view the Kaga Plain and the Sea of Japan, spending an open, refreshing time in the clear air. At night, a sky full of stars is another highlight.
quiz_en: If you went camping at a highland spot like Okuradake Kogen, which constellation would you want to look for in the night sky?

desc_en: You have arrived at Aramata Gorge in Akasemachi, Komatsu City. This gorge was carved through the mountains by the Gogo River, with a clear stream flowing between the rocks and green trees covering both banks. In summer many people come seeking coolness, and in autumn the gorge is colored with autumn leaves. Akase Dam is also nearby, making it a place to slowly savor the nature of Komatsu's mountain villages.
quiz_en: If you visited a mountain gorge like Aramata, how would you like to spend your time beside the clear stream?

desc_en: You have arrived at Komatsu Tenmangu in Tenjinmachi, Komatsu City. Founded in the Edo period by Maeda Toshitsune, the third lord of the Kaga domain, it enshrines Sugawara no Michizane, the god of learning. It stands on the banks of the Kakehashi River, and many people visit to pray for success in exams. Plum trees are planted in the grounds, and their blossoms color the shrine in early spring.
quiz_en: Who was the third lord of the Kaga domain who founded Komatsu Tenmangu, a shrine dedicated to the god of learning?

desc_en: You have arrived at Awazu Onsen in Komatsu City. Said to have been opened by Taicho, who founded worship on Mount Hakusan in the Nara period, it is one of the old hot spring resorts of Hokuriku, and long-established inns with long histories still guard its waters. The hot spring town also has a public bath called the soyu, where you can easily enjoy a soak. Wrapped in the steam of Kaga, feel the history of waters spanning more than a thousand years.
quiz_en: Who was the Nara-period monk, known for opening Mount Hakusan, who is said to have founded Awazu Onsen in Kaga?

desc_en: You have arrived at Kiba Onsen in Kibamachi, Komatsu City. Nearby Kibagata is a lagoon where rich waterside nature remains, with walking paths circling it, and on clear days you can see snowcapped Mount Hakusan beyond the water. On the shores of this lagoon, where you can enjoy the scenery of all four seasons, soak in the hot water at leisure and soothe the fatigue of your journey.
quiz_en: From the shores of Kibagata in Komatsu, which sacred mountain can you see beyond the surface of the water on a clear day?

desc_en: You have arrived at Akoudani Onsen in Nakaumimachi, Komatsu City. This onsen (hot spring) lies in a valley leading from the Kaga Plain into the mountains on the outskirts of Komatsu. Komatsu prospered as a key town of Kaga Province and is also known for producing Kutani ware. Warm up slowly in this quiet valley hot spring, and after your bath, continue your journey exploring the traditional crafts of Kaga.
quiz_en: If you chose Kutani ware as a souvenir in Komatsu, where this pottery is made, what kind of dish or vessel would you want?

desc_en: You have arrived at Shiroyone Senmaida in Wajima City. On a steep slope facing the Sea of Japan, small rice paddies stack up layer upon layer, and this landscape uniting sea and paddies symbolizes Noto. It is also recognized as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System as part of Noto's Satoyama and Satoumi. It was damaged in the Noto Peninsula Earthquake, but restoration is moving forward thanks to the people who care for it.
quiz_en: What international heritage designation has been given to Noto's Satoyama and Satoumi, which includes the Shiroyone Senmaida rice terraces?

desc_en: You have arrived at Hegurajima in Wajima City. This small island floats in the Sea of Japan far north of Wajima Port and has long been known as a base for ama free diving. Although it is a small, flat island, it becomes a stopover for migratory birds in spring and autumn, making it a dream destination for birdwatchers where many rare birds can be observed. Savor the clear sea and quiet time.
quiz_en: What is the traditional form of fishing long handed down on Hegurajima, in which divers go under the sea to gather abalone and turban shells?

desc_en: You have arrived at the Wajima hot spring area in Wajima City. Wajima is known for producing Wajima-nuri, durable and beautiful lacquerware, and inns are scattered around Kawaimachi and other parts of the city center. The Noto Peninsula Earthquake caused severe damage to the town, including the morning market street, but its people continue working toward recovery. While soaking in the hot water, reflect on the handicraft culture of this lacquer town.
quiz_en: What is the name of Wajima's durable lacquerware, made by applying many coats over a base that uses local diatomaceous earth?

desc_en: You have arrived at Nebuta Onsen in Onomachi, Wajima City. This onsen (hot spring) lies on the Sea of Japan side a little away from central Wajima, letting you enjoy the bath in quiet seaside surroundings. Noto's outer coast, the Sotoura, is a varied coastline where rough waves crash in winter. In waters loved by local people, warm your body as you feel the sea breeze of Noto.
quiz_en: After a soak at an onsen on the seashore of Noto's outer coast, what winter seafood would you like to taste locally?

desc_en: You have arrived at Cape Saruyama in Monzen, Wajima City. Jutting out into the Sotoura on the western side of the Noto Peninsula, this cape is a dramatic scenic spot with cliffs plunging into the Sea of Japan. In early spring, yukiwariso (hepatica) grow in clusters on the slopes and bloom with dainty flowers, and a lighthouse stands atop the cape. Gazing at the grand panorama of the Sea of Japan below, feel both the harshness and the beauty of Noto's nature.
quiz_en: What dainty flower grows in clusters on the slopes of Cape Saruyama in early spring, peeking out from the melting snow?

desc_en: You have arrived at the grand festival of Tsurugiji Hachiman Shrine in Tsurugiji, Monzen, Wajima City. Tsurugiji is a settlement facing the Sea of Japan on the western side of the Noto Peninsula. Noto festivals often feature large lanterns called kiriko and mikoshi (portable shrines), and the whole community turns out to support them. As lights glow in the darkness of night and chants echo all around, feel the passion of Noto's people for their festivals.
quiz_en: At festivals in Noto, what are the large, tall lanterns called that are lit up and carried through the streets by many people?

desc_en: You have arrived at Suzu Onsen in Horyumachi, Suzu City. Suzu, at the tip of the Noto Peninsula, is a land with both a calm inner coast and a rugged outer coast. Off Horyumachi floats Mitsukejima, also called Gunkanjima (Battleship Island) for its shape, one of Noto's representative scenic spots. Relax in the hot springs of this town at the end of the land, where you can feel the sea.
quiz_en: What is the name of the island floating off Horyumachi in Suzu City that is also known as Battleship Island because of its shape?

desc_en: You have arrived at Yoshigaura Onsen in Jike, Misaki, Suzu City. This seaside onsen (hot spring) at the tip of the Noto Peninsula, close to Cape Rokkozaki, has an inn lit by lamps that conveys the charm of a hidden hot spring. It stands quietly at the back of a cove surrounded by cliffs, and its appeal is a stillness where only the sound of the waves can be heard. Spend a night at the end of the land in soft lamplight.
quiz_en: At a hidden hot spring on the tip of the Noto Peninsula, what sound would you like to hear during a night spent under lamplight?

desc_en: You have arrived at Hachigasaki Onsen in Suzu City. The nearby Hachigasaki coast is a beautiful shoreline of white sand that bustles with swimmers in summer. Suzu, at the tip of the Noto Peninsula, is also known for agehama-style salt making, produced using traditional methods. Along with the open seaside scenery, slowly soothe your fatigue in the hot water.
quiz_en: What is the traditional method handed down on the Suzu coast in which seawater is spread over sand and dried by the sun to make salt?

desc_en: You have arrived at the Kiriko Festival in Jike, Misaki, Suzu City. From summer to autumn, kiriko festivals are held all over Noto, with large lanterns called kiriko carried through the streets by many people. The kiriko of Jike are known for being especially large, and the sight of their lights towering into the night sky and illuminating the village is overwhelming. Savor a festival night when the people of Noto are at their most passionate of the year.
quiz_en: At the Jike Kiriko Festival, about how many people do you think it takes to carry one of the giant kiriko that tower into the night sky?

desc_en: You have arrived at Yamashiro Onsen in Kaga City. Said to have been founded by the monk Gyoki in the Nara period, it is one of Hokuriku's leading hot spring resorts, with the public bath Soyu and the Kosoyu, restored to its Meiji-era appearance, at the center of town. The townscape, where inns and shops surround the baths, is called Yu no Kuruwa. It is also associated with Kitaoji Rosanjin, and a culture of tableware such as Kutani ware lives on here.
quiz_en: In the center of Yamashiro Onsen, what is the townscape called where inns and shops are arranged around the public bath?

desc_en: You have arrived at Yamanaka Onsen in Kaga City. This hot spring resort spreads along Kakusenkei, the gorge of the Daishoji River, where Matsuo Basho stayed for a long time during his Oku no Hosomichi journey and praised its fine waters. Across the gorge stretch the all-cypress Korogi Bridge and the S-shaped Ayatori Bridge, and you can enjoy walks along the trail. It is also the home of Yamanaka lacquerware, showcasing the art of wood turning.
quiz_en: What is the name of the charming bridge made entirely of Japanese cypress that spans Kakusenkei Gorge at Yamanaka Onsen?

desc_en: You have arrived at Zensho-ji in Daishoji, Kaga City. This Soto Zen temple is associated with the Yamaguchi family, lords of the Daishoji domain, and its Rakan Hall houses statues of the Five Hundred Arhats, each with a different expression that draws you in. It is also known as the temple where Matsuo Basho and his disciple Sora stayed during their Oku no Hosomichi journey. Visit it together with the calm streets of the castle town of Daishoji.
quiz_en: How many arhat statues are the Rakan Hall of Zensho-ji known for housing, each one with its own unique expression?

desc_en: You have arrived at Katayamazu Onsen in Kaga City. This hot spring resort spreads along the shores of Shibayamagata, with inns lining the lakeside and a view of sacred Mount Hakusan across the water. On clear days the snowcapped form of Hakusan is reflected in the lake, and the lake's changing expressions from morning to evening are part of its charm. Stroll the lakeside path and savor the atmosphere unique to a waterside hot spring resort.
quiz_en: What is the name of the lake along whose shores Katayamazu Onsen spreads, offering views of Mount Hakusan across the water?

desc_en: You have arrived at Shibayama Onsen in Shibayamamachi, Kaga City. This onsen (hot spring) is on the shores of Shibayamagata, letting you enjoy the bath amid quiet waterside scenery. Waterfowl gather on the lagoon, and on clear days you can see Mount Hakusan in the distance. Close to the center of the Kaga hot spring area, it is a calm hot spring where you can relax while gazing at the lake.
quiz_en: At this onsen on the shores of Shibayamagata, what scene would you most like to see reflected on the surface of the lake?

desc_en: You have arrived at Ochigata in Hakui City. This lagoon spreads at the base of the Noto Peninsula, surrounded by plains and farmland. In winter, many tundra swans fly in from the north, and it is known as a wintering site where they can be seen resting in the rice paddies and on the water. The winter sight of flocks of white birds dancing in the sky is a seasonal tradition of Hakui.
quiz_en: What large white migratory bird flies in flocks from the north to spend the winter at Ochigata Lagoon?

desc_en: You have arrived at Keta Taisha in Hakui City. As the ichinomiya (highest-ranked shrine) of Noto Province, it has long been revered, enshrining Okuninushi no Mikoto, and many visitors come to pray to him as a god of matchmaking. Behind the shrine buildings spreads the Irazu no Mori (Forbidden Forest), where people have been forbidden to enter since ancient times, filling the place with a sacred air. In these grounds near the Sea of Japan, pray for a good match.
quiz_en: What is the forest called that spreads behind the buildings of Keta Taisha, where people have been forbidden to enter since ancient times?

desc_en: You have arrived at Yoko-ji in Sakaimachi, Hakui City. This ancient temple was founded in the Kamakura period by Keizan Jokin of the Soto Zen school, and its buildings stand quietly in the mountains of Noto. Walking the approach surrounded by cedar groves, you can feel the crisp air typical of a Zen temple. Savor the charm of a mountain temple that shows a different face each season, from fresh green and autumn leaves to snowy scenes.
quiz_en: Who was the Kamakura-period monk who founded Yoko-ji and played a major role in the development of the Soto Zen school?

desc_en: You have arrived at the Five-Story Pagoda Festival held at Myojo-ji in Takidanimachi, Hakui City. Myojo-ji is a renowned Nichiren-sect temple whose halls and pagoda were developed under the patronage of the Maeda family of the Kaga domain, and its five-story pagoda rising amid the greenery is its symbol. On festival day, many people gather in the grounds, filling them with an unusual liveliness. Enjoy the festive atmosphere against the backdrop of these historic buildings.
quiz_en: If you looked up at the five-story pagoda of Myojo-ji, from which angle would you try to take your best photo of it?

desc_en: You have arrived at Mount Hakusan in Hakusan City. Rising 2,702 meters on the border between Ishikawa and Gifu, it is counted among Japan's Three Holy Mountains, along with Mount Fuji and Tateyama. It is said to have been opened by Taicho in the Nara period and is the source of faith for Hakusan shrines across Japan. In summer, alpine plants bearing the Hakusan name bloom across the summit area, and it bustles with climbers coming to worship the sunrise.
quiz_en: Which mountain straddling Ishikawa and Gifu prefectures is counted among Japan's Three Holy Mountains along with Mount Fuji and Tateyama?
